problem.title: Wheatstone bridge (Engine B flagship)
problem.text:
A 10 V battery drives a bridge: 10 ohm and 20 ohm in the left arm, 20 ohm and 10 ohm
in the right arm, and a 10 ohm bridge wire between the two midpoints. No formula
isolates the bridge current -- it takes the assembled Kirchhoff system. What flows
through the bridge resistor?

because.detail: An ideal source of constant emf. Two terminals; current leaves the positive one. Ideal here means zero internal resistance, which the assumption list on every formula states plainly.

A point of one potential in a circuit — a junction where branches meet. Engine B (nodal assembly) solves for its potential with Kirchhoff's current law; branches declare `terminal_a`/`terminal_b` relations to the nodes they join, and a battery declares `positive_terminal`/`negative_terminal`. Created by wiring, like the pairs.
